factual_sources.text:
Review Cycle

Northstar runs formal performance reviews twice per year: mid-year review in June and year-end review in December. Managers should collect evidence throughout the review period instead of relying only on recent events.

Performance Documentation

Performance feedback should include specific examples, business impact, expected behavior, and follow-up actions. Managers should avoid vague labels and should distinguish between skill gaps, behavior concerns, and role mismatch.

Performance Improvement Process

When serious performance issues continue after feedback, managers should consult People Operations before starting a formal performance improvement process. Documentation should include expectations, timeline, support offered, and review checkpoints.

This guide does not contain salary bands or compensation formulas.

Access Notice

This document is restricted to Managers. It contains manager-only performance and promotion process guidance.

Promotion Calibration

Promotion calibration is reviewed by managers and department leadership. Employees should not be promised a promotion before calibration is complete.

One-on-One Expectations

Managers should hold one-on-one meetings with direct reports at least every two weeks. Notes should focus on priorities, blockers, feedback, and growth needs. Sensitive personal details should not be recorded unless required for an HR process.

Office Expectations

Hybrid teams should define collaboration days at least one month in advance. Employees should attend required team planning, onboarding, incident review, and customer workshop sessions in person when asked by their manager.

Employee Support Channels

General HR questions should be sent to People Operations. Benefits questions should be sent to the benefits support queue. Security access questions should be sent to IT Support. Performance or role expectation questions should first be discussed with the employee's manager.

Team Planning

Managers should maintain a quarterly team plan with goals, ownership, dependencies, and risks. Plans should identify customer-impacting work, hiring assumptions, and capacity constraints.
